mainTopic: Why the ערכין משנה uses only Jewish examples, and how a consecrated field with trees is redeemed (רב הונא vs. רב נחמן)
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of why the earlier משנה gave only Jewish examples. One answer is that it quietly teaches the ban on saying 'how beautiful is this gentile' and prefers to stay within one nation. Another answer is that its later clause, שדה אחוזה, only applies to Jews. Then a new משנה teaches that a שדה אחוזה is redeemed at a fixed 50 shekels per בית זרע חומר שעורים, whether the land is poor or excellent, while a שדה מקנה is redeemed at its real value. רבי אליעזר disagrees: both fields use the fixed price, and only the שדה אחוזה adds a חומש. In the גמרא, רב הונא rules that trees in a consecrated field are redeemed at their value and the land separately, because a person consecrates generously. רב נחמן challenges him three times, from the משנה and from two ברייתות. The גמרא answers the last challenge by saying that ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who holds a consecrator gives stingily. It then questions that answer, because רבי שמעון follows the time of פדיון, and it brings a ברייתא about a son who bought his father's field to prove this. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה avoids praising a gentile's beauty
steps.stepSummary: The משנה avoided a gentile example in order to teach, in passing, רב יהודה's rule in the name of רב: it is forbidden to say 'how beautiful is this gentile.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is teaching us something extra along the way, following רב יהודה in the name of רב: a person may not say 'How beautiful is this gentile.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה did not use a gentile in its example of beauty. The answer is that it is quietly teaching a separate rule: you may not praise a gentile's looks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have said 'the most beautiful gentile,' but that wording would itself praise a gentile's beauty. By leaving it out, the משנה hints at רב יהודה's prohibition. So the משנה's wording carries a second lesson besides the laws of ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter taught in passing, a side lesson
It teaches us
Forbidden
Beautiful, attractive

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a משנה's choice of wording can hide a separate הלכה. Here that הלכה is the rule against praising a gentile's beauty.

phrases.aramaic: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: It teaches us a matter in passing,
in line with what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
for Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is forbidden for a person to say
'How beautiful is this gentile.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of why the משנה gave no gentile example
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording is deliberate and teaches a side הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have used a gentile to show the full range of people
steps.terutzMaskana: It avoided 'beautiful gentile' so as to hint at the prohibition of praising a gentile's beauty

steps.title: Then use a beautiful Jew and an ugly gentile
steps.stepSummary: If the only problem was praising a gentile, the משנה could have said 'the most beautiful in Israel and the ugliest among gentiles.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה say: 'the most beautiful in Israel and the ugliest among the gentiles'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Calling a gentile ugly is not praise, so the משנה could still have included a gentile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer only explains why the משנה avoided a beautiful gentile. It does not explain why there is no gentile at all. An ugly gentile would show an even wider range without breaking רב יהודה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it teach
Ugly, unsightly

phrases.english: But let it teach: 'the most beautiful in Israel
and the ugliest among the gentiles'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the gentile was left out only because of רב יהודה's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ugly gentile would not break the rule, so a gentile could still have been included

steps.title: The משנה stays within one nation
steps.stepSummary: The משנה prefers to give examples from one nation, not to mix two nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה deals with one nation; it does not deal with two nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's style is to compare people within a single nation. That is why it did not set a Jew against a gentile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for leaving out the gentile is now a matter of style, not of halacha. Both of the משנה's examples come from within Israel, so a gentile would not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: One nation
It is dealing with
Two nations

phrases.english: It deals with one nation;
it does not deal with two nations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could freely compare a Jew with a gentile
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה limits its comparisons to one nation

steps.title: But the משנה compares כהנים and ישראלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'one nation' rule using a later משנה that compares a woman from the כהונה with a woman from Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It doesn't deal with two groups? But the משנה teaches: 'the most prominent woman in the כהונה and the lowliest in Israel'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back by pointing to another case where the משנה does compare two different groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the law of the fine for אונס and מפתה, the משנה sets a כהנת beside an ordinary Jewish woman. That looks like two separate groups, which would go against the claim that the משנה only compares within one group.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches
Priesthood
Lowliest, least prominent

phrases.english: And it doesn't?
But it teaches:
the most prominent woman in the priesthood
phrases.notes: This comes from the משנה on 14b about the fine paid to a girl who was forced or seduced.

phrases.english: and the lowliest in Israel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the משנה deals with only one nation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה compares כהנים and ישראלים, which seem to be two separate groups

steps.title: כהנים and ישראלים are one nation
steps.stepSummary: כהנים and ישראלים are one nation. The only difference is that כהנים have more קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is one nation. It is just that כהנים are holier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a כהן and a ישראל both belong to the Jewish people, so that משנה is still talking about one nation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between כהנים and ישראלים is a level of קדושה, not a different nationality. So the 'one nation' rule still stands, and a gentile example would have broken it.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness, sanctity
More

phrases.english: There it is one nation;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִקְדָּישׁ הוּא דְּקַדִּישִׁי כֹּהֲנִים טְפֵי.
phrases.english: it is only that the priests are holier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: two levels of holiness, one nation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כהנים and ישראלים count as two separate groups
steps.terutzMaskana: They are one nation, so the משנה's style holds

steps.title: Second answer: the later clause about an ancestral field
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the משנה uses only Jews because its later clause about שדה אחוזה only applies to Jews, since gentiles do not have an ancestral portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: since the משנה later wants to teach about a שדה אחוזה, which exists only for Jews and not for gentiles, who have no אחוזה, it teaches all its cases about Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason why the משנה kept to Jewish examples. It points to the משנה's later clause, which only makes sense for Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שדה אחוזה is land a family received as its portion in ארץ ישראל, and gentiles have no such portion. Since that later case must be about Jews, the משנה kept all of its cases about Jews to stay consistent. This answer does not need the 'one nation' rule at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: an alternative answer
Since, because it was already
The later clause of a משנה
An ancestral field inherited from the original division of the land

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives no gentile example for two possible reasons. It is either hinting at the ban on praising a gentile's beauty and keeping to one nation, or keeping all its cases about Jews because of the שדה אחוזה clause.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
since it wants to teach
in the later clause 'an ancestral field,'
which you find only among Jews,
and you do not find it with a gentile,
since they are not people who have an ancestral portion,
for this reason it teaches it about Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the challenge of step 2, instead of the one-nation answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Consistency with a later clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could have used a gentile in the ערכין examples
steps.terutzMaskana: All its cases are about Jews because the שדה אחוזה case can only be about Jews

steps.title: The fixed redemption price for an inherited field
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a שדה אחוזה is always redeemed at 50 shekels per בית זרע חומר שעורים, whether the land is poor or excellent. A שדה מקנה is redeemed at its actual value.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With an inherited field, the fixed price can work out lenient or strict. How so? Whether someone consecrates poor sandy land around the city or the fine orchards of סבסטי, he pays 50 silver shekels for each area that would be sown with a חומר of barley. But for a bought field, he pays what it is actually worth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the earlier clause about שדה אחוזה. The price to redeem it is fixed by the תורה and does not depend on how good the land is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lenient' means the owner of a great orchard pays only the fixed 50 shekels, which is less than its worth. 'Strict' means the owner of poor sandy land still pays the full 50 shekels, which is more than its worth. A שדה מקנה does not get the fixed price; it is valued like any other item.

keyTerms.meaning: An inherited field, the family's ancestral portion in ארץ ישראל
A purchased field, not inherited
To be lenient and to be strict: the same rule can help or hurt
The area of land you would plant with a חומר (a large measure) of barley seed
Its actual market value

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the fixed price is always a discount. For excellent land it is a bargain, but for poor land it costs more than the land is worth. That is why the משנה calls it both lenient and strict.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
With an ancestral field, there is leniency and strictness.
How so?
Both one who consecrates in the sands of the surrounding area,
phrases.notes: The poor, sandy land around the city, which is worth very little.

phrases.english: and one who consecrates in the orchards of Sebastia,
gives, for an area sown with a kor of barley,
fifty silver shekels.
And with a purchased field, he gives its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה that spells out the שדה אחוזה clause mentioned in the earlier משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שדה אחוזה is redeemed at a fixed 50 shekels per בית זרע חומר שעורים no matter its quality; a שדה מקנה is redeemed at its value.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: both fields have the fixed price, only the fifth is different
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that both a שדה מקנה and a שדה אחוזה are redeemed at the fixed price. The only difference is that the חומש is added for a שדה אחוזה and not for a שדה מקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: A bought field and an inherited field are the same, both at the fixed price. So what is the difference between them? With an inherited field he adds a fifth, and with a bought field he does not add a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה about the bought field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said a שדה מקנה is redeemed at its real value. רבי אליעזר says it also uses the fixed 50-shekel rate. To keep some difference between the two fields, he says the extra חומש applies only to the שדה אחוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra fifth added on top of the redemption price
What is the difference between
Both this and that, meaning they are treated the same

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה וְאֶחָד שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה,
phrases.english: Both a purchased field and an ancestral field are the same.
phrases.notes: He means both are redeemed at the fixed 50 shekels.

phrases.aramaic: מָה בֵּין שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה לִשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה?
phrases.english: What is the difference between an ancestral field and a purchased field?
That with an ancestral field he gives a fifth,
and with a purchased field he does not give a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה וְאֶחָד שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion about the שדה מקנה rule in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both fields are redeemed at the fixed price; only a שדה אחוזה adds a חומש.
steps.whatToRemember: First opinion: inherited field = fixed price, bought field = real value. רבי אליעזר: both = fixed price, and only the inherited field adds a חומש.

steps.title: רב הונא: trees and land are redeemed separately
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that when a field full of trees is consecrated, the trees are redeemed at their value and then the land at the fixed price. The גמרא infers that he holds a person consecrates generously.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא said: If someone consecrated a field full of trees, when he redeems it, he redeems the trees at their value, and then he redeems the land at 50 silver shekels for each area sown with a חומר of barley. So it seems רב הונא holds that when a person consecrates, he consecrates generously.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new ruling about a consecrated field with trees on it. The גמרא then works out the idea behind his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the trees are just part of the field and are covered by the fixed price. רב הונא says the trees are counted separately and paid at full value. The reason is that a person who consecrates gives generously, so he meant to give the trees as their own item, not just as part of the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeems, buys back from הקדש
Trees
The land itself
It follows that, so we see that
He consecrates with a generous eye, giving in the fullest way

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge. The משנה said even orchards pay only the fixed price, which seems to clash with paying for trees separately.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Huna said:
If one consecrated a field full of trees,
when he redeems them,
he redeems the trees at their value,
and then goes back and redeems the land
for an area sown with a kor of barley
at fifty silver shekels.
Evidently Rav Huna holds:
When a person consecrates, he consecrates generously.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הִקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֶה מְלֵיאָה אִילָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens with an אמורא's ruling about a case connected to the משנה's fixed price.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trees in a consecrated field are redeemed at their value, then the land at the fixed rate, because a person consecrates generously.

steps.title: רב נחמן challenges from the orchards in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן points out that the משנה says even the orchards of סבסטי are redeemed only at the fixed price. That suggests the trees are not paid for separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged רב הונא: The משנה says that whether someone consecrates poor sandy land or the orchards of סבסטי, he pays 50 silver shekels for each area sown with a חומר of barley!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב הונא's ruling using the words of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Orchards are full of trees. If the trees were redeemed separately, as רב הונא says, the משנה should not say the orchard costs only the fixed 50 shekels. So the משנה seems to show that the trees are included in the land's fixed price.

keyTerms.meaning: The sandy land around the city, which is poor-quality land
The fine orchards of Sebastia, which are excellent land
Fifty silver shekels, the fixed redemption price

phrases.english: Rav Nahman challenged Rav Huna:
Both one who consecrates in the sands of the surrounding area,
and one who consecrates in the orchards of Sebastia,
gives, for an area sown with a kor of barley,
fifty silver shekels!
phrases.notes: Just the fixed price and nothing extra for the trees. That is the problem for רב הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling in step 9 from the משנה in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that trees are redeemed separately at their value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives only the fixed price for orchards, which are full of trees. So the trees must be included in the land, not redeemed separately.

steps.title: רב הונא: the משנה means land fit for orchards
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה's orchards of סבסטי means land good enough for orchards, not land that actually has trees on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: I say the משנה is talking about land that is fit for orchards.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his ruling by reading the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is only comparing the worst land with the best land. It means excellent soil that could grow orchards, but it has no trees planted on it yet. So there are no trees to pay for separately, and רב הונא's ruling still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for, suitable for
Land good enough for orchards, but without trees planted on it
I am saying, this is what is meant

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: trees are redeemed at their value and the land at the fixed price. The משנה's 'orchards' means land fit for orchards, with no trees on it yet.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am speaking of land fit for orchards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's orchards of סבסטי are fields with trees, so the trees must be covered by the fixed price.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means excellent land fit for orchards with no trees on it, so it does not contradict separate payment for trees.

steps.title: A ברייתא includes tree fields in the fixed price
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a ברייתא that learns from the word 'שדה' that fields of vines, reeds and trees are also redeemed by the fixed-price rule of בית זרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged רב הונא: The פסוק says 'an area of sowing.' That covers only a sowing field. How do we know the rule also covers a field of vines, a field of reeds, or a field of trees? The פסוק says 'שדה,' which means any field.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a second challenge against רב הונא. He uses a ברייתא that puts tree fields under the same fixed price as plain sowing land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the trees are paid for at their value and only the land is paid at the fixed price. This ברייתא says a שדה אילנות falls under the fixed-price rule. That sounds like the whole field, trees included, costs only the fixed price.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of land measured by how much seed it takes to sow it
A field full of trees, an orchard
The פסוק teaches us (it introduces the source)
In any case, any kind of field

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is challenging רב הונא again.

phrases.english: "An area of sowing" —
I would only know about an area of sowing;
a field of vines and a field of reeds
and a field of trees, from where do we know?
The verse says "field": any field at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב הונא answered the first challenge from the orchards of סבסטי, רב נחמן brings a new source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that trees in a consecrated field are redeemed separately at their value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts a field of trees under the fixed-price rule. That suggests the trees are included in the fixed price and not paid for on their own.

steps.title: Pay for the trees first, then the land
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the ברייתא also means the person first redeems the trees at their value and then redeems the land at the fixed price.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: Here too, he redeems the trees and then redeems the land again.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his ruling. He reads the ברייתא so that it fits with his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only teaches that a tree field also has its land redeemed at the fixed price. It does not say the trees are free. So the person pays for the trees first, and then pays the fixed price for the land.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeems, and then redeems again: two separate payments
Here too

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here too
he redeems, and then redeems again.
phrases.notes: First he pays for the trees at their value. Then he pays the fixed price for the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a tree field is entirely covered by the fixed price.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means the land of a tree field is redeemed at the fixed price. The trees are still paid for separately first.

steps.title: Three trees bring the land and the trees between them
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a ברייתא: if someone consecrates three trees planted ten per בית סאה, the land and the trees between them are also consecrated, and he redeems at the fixed price. With a different density, or if he consecrated them one at a time, only the trees themselves are consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged him again: If someone consecrated three trees that are planted at a rate of ten trees per בית סאה, he has consecrated the land and the trees between them too. When he redeems, he redeems at the rate of 50 silver shekels for an area that takes a חומר of barley seed. If the trees were planted closer than that, or farther apart than that, or if he consecrated them one after another, he has not consecrated the land or the trees between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a third challenge against רב הונא. This ברייתא describes a case where trees and land are consecrated together and redeemed at the fixed price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the normal planting case, the land and the trees between them all become consecrated. The ברייתא then says he redeems at the fixed price of 50 shekels and says nothing about paying for the trees separately. That seems to go against רב הונא. The גמרא's answer comes after this.

keyTerms.meaning: An area that takes one סאה of seed to sow
A planting, here meaning how close together the trees are planted
The land itself
One after another, each tree separately
Fifty silver shekels, the fixed price from the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: The 'trees between them' are not the three trees he named. They are other trees growing in the land around them. They come along only because the land is consecrated.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
If one consecrated three trees
in a planting of ten trees per בית סאה —
he has consecrated the land
and the trees between them,
when he redeems, he redeems
an area for sowing a חומר of barley
for fifty silver shekels.

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִיכֵּן, אוֹ יָתֵר עַל כֵּן,
phrases.english: If less than this, or more than this,
or if he consecrated them one after another —
he has not consecrated

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַקַּרְקַע וְלֹא אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: neither the land nor the trees between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: איתיביה הקדיש שלשה אילנות ממטע עשרה לבית סאה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב הונא answered the second challenge, רב נחמן brings a third source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that trees are redeemed separately at their value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the land and the trees between them are redeemed at the fixed price of 50 shekels. It never mentions a separate payment for the trees, which suggests they are included in the fixed price.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא: trees first, then land
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's ברייתא continues: even if he consecrated the trees and only later the land, he redeems the trees at their value and then the land at the fixed price.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that: even if he consecrated his trees first and the land afterward, when he redeems them he redeems the trees at their value, and then he redeems the land at the fixed price: an area for sowing a חומר of barley for fifty silver שקלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from step 14. This second half describes a case where trees and land were consecrated at two separate times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the trees were consecrated on their own, so they are redeemed on their own at their real value. Only after that is the land redeemed at the fixed price. The ברייתא spells out two separate payments here, and the next step builds on that.

keyTerms.meaning: And more than that; introduces a bigger case
Trees
At their actual value
And then he redeems again (a second, separate payment)
An area that takes a חומר of barley seed to plant; the fixed unit for redeeming a field

phrases.english: And moreover, even
if he consecrated its trees,
phrases.notes: This means trees that were not part of the first case, like trees planted closer or farther apart, or consecrated one at a time.

phrases.english: and afterward he consecrated the land,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדֶה — פּוֹדֶה אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בְּשׇׁוְויֵהֶן,
phrases.english: when he redeems, he redeems the trees at their value,
and then he redeems the land:
an area for sowing a חומר of barley
for fifty silver shekels!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that רב נחמן began quoting in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that trees are always redeemed separately at their value.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second half of the ברייתא says outright that there are two payments when trees and land were consecrated separately. This sets up a contrast with the first half, which does not say so.

steps.title: Why the first half cannot also mean two payments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks an easy answer: since only the second half says 'redeem and then redeem again,' the first half must mean a single fixed-price payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too, in the first half, he redeems and then redeems again: since the second half says 'he redeems and then redeems again,' this shows that the first half does not mean that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts down the kind of answer רב הונא gave in step 13 to a different ברייתא: that 'redeemed at the fixed price' really means trees first and then land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first half also meant two payments, the ברייתא would not need to say 'and then redeems again' only in the second half. Because it says this only there, the first half must mean the fixed price covers the land and the trees together. That goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; brings up a possible answer in order to reject it
By inference; this shows that
The first half of a teaching
The second half of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: This is a reading from contrast: the proof comes from what the first half does NOT say, compared with what the second half does say.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
here too he redeems and then redeems again,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the first half of the ברייתא, the case of three trees per בית סאה.

phrases.english: but since the latter clause says he redeems and then redeems again,
this shows that the first clause does not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the second half (step 15) to block רב הונא's usual answer from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's way of reading 'fixed price' as two payments.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second half says 'two payments' outright and the first half does not, so the first half must mean one fixed payment for everything.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון: a consecrator gives stingily
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who holds that a person who consecrates gives 'with a stingy eye.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי שמעון, who says that a person who consecrates does so with a stingy eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא follows only רבי שמעון. רב הונא can follow the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, someone who consecrates holds back as much as he can. So he does not give the trees as an item of their own; they come along only as part of the land, and the fixed land price covers them. רב הונא's rule, that trees are paid for separately, follows the opposite view, that a person consecrates generously.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
With a stingy eye; giving as little as possible
One who consecrates something to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rather, whose view is this?
It is רבי שמעון, who says:
one who consecrates, consecrates with a stingy eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 14-16 by assigning the ברייתא to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to one תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that everyone agrees trees are covered by the fixed price, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון's 'stingy eye' rule. רב הונא can follow the view of the רבנן.

steps.title: The source for רבי שמעון's stingy-eye view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute: the רבנן say consecrating a field includes everything in it, while רבי שמעון says only a grafted carob tree and a sycamore stump are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: one who consecrates a field has consecrated all of it. רבי שמעון says: he consecrated only the grafted carob tree and the sycamore stump.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי שמעון really holds the stingy-eye view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say a field consecrated without details includes everything in it, trees too. רבי שמעון says it includes only a grafted carob and a sycamore stump. Rashi explains why: they are very old and big, and they draw from the consecrated field more than other trees do. Other trees stay with the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: A grafted carob tree
The stump of a sycamore tree, which grows back from the cut trunk
He consecrated all of it

phrases.english: As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה — הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: One who consecrates a field has consecrated all of it.
רבי שמעון says:
he consecrated only
the grafted carob tree and the sycamore stump.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view credited to רבי שמעון in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a consecrator gives with a stingy eye.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about consecrating a field, which shows the disagreement between the רבנן and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: consecrating a field includes everything in it. רבי שמעון: a consecrator gives stingily, so only things that are part of the ground, like a grafted carob and a sycamore stump, are included.

steps.title: Testing the רבי שמעון answer against the second half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new difficulty: if the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, look at its second half again, where trees and land are redeemed separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי שמעון, read the second half: and moreover, even if he consecrated his trees and afterward the land, when he redeems he redeems the trees at their value and then redeems the land at an area for sowing a חומר of barley for fifty silver שקלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes the second half of the ברייתא again to check whether it really fits רבי שמעון. The actual problem is explained in the lines that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is quoting the same second half from step 15 for a new reason. Before, it was used to attack רב הונא. Now it is used to test the answer that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: If; here it tests whether an answer really works
Read the second half; look at what it says

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a repeat of step 15. The same words are quoted again for a new purpose: to test the answer from step 17.

phrases.english: If it is רבי שמעון, say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹתָיו
phrases.english: and moreover, even if he consecrated its trees
and afterward he consecrated the land,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדֶה — פּוֹדֶה אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בְּשׇׁוְויֵהֶן,
phrases.english: when he redeems, he redeems the trees at their value,
and then he redeems

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף.
phrases.english: an area for sowing a חומר of barley for fifty silver shekels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer from step 17 by going back to the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא suggests the second half may not fit רבי שמעון's stingy-eye view. The exact problem is spelled out in the text that follows.

steps.title: If this follows רבי שמעון, the trees should be redeemed together with the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי שמעון judges a field by its status at the time of פדיון. So the trees should go along with the land at the fixed price, not be redeemed separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, we should look at the time of redemption, and the trees should be redeemed along with their land. After all, we know that רבי שמעון looks at the time of redemption!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the answer from Step 17. If the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, its second half does not fit his known approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the ברייתא says that trees consecrated first and land consecrated later are redeemed separately. But by the time of פדיון, both the trees and the land are already הקדש. If רבי שמעון judges by the time of פדיון, the trees should just be included with the land at the fixed price.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: buying a consecrated item back from הקדש
Let him follow / go according to (a certain moment or factor)
Along with, as part of
For we have heard that he holds (we know his opinion from elsewhere)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new question, separate from the 'stingy eye' idea in Step 17. That idea was about what is included when he consecrates. This question is about which moment counts when he redeems: the time of consecration or the time of פדיון.

phrases.english: And if it is רבי שמעון —
phrases.notes: He means: if רב נחמן's ברייתא really follows רבי שמעון, as Step 17 said.

phrases.english: let him follow the time of redemption,
and let them be redeemed along with their land,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the trees, which by now are consecrated together with the land.

phrases.english: for we have heard regarding רבי שמעון
that he follows the time of redemption!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — לֵיזִיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the difficulty opened in Step 19 about the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 17 that רב נחמן's ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון judges by the time of פדיון. At פדיון, both the trees and the land are consecrated, so they should be redeemed together at the fixed price. The ברייתא's separate redemption contradicts this.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a son who bought his father's field and consecrated it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי שמעון follows the time of פדיון. A son bought a field from his father, consecrated it, and then the father died. A פסוק teaches that the field is treated like a שדה אחוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: From where do we know about someone who bought a field from his father and consecrated it, and afterward his father died, that it is treated for him like an ancestral field? The verse says: 'If a field that he bought, which is not of his ancestral field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving its source for the claim that רבי שמעון follows the time of פדיון. It quotes a ברייתא and the פסוק it learns from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he consecrated it, the field was only a purchased field (שדה מקנה). By the time he comes to redeem it, his father has died, so it would have been his by inheritance anyway. The ברייתא treats it as a שדה אחוזה, so its status later on is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we know this)? Asking for a source
An ancestral field, inherited family land, redeemed at a fixed price by the תורה
A purchased field, redeemed at its market value
He consecrated it to הקדש
The verse teaches. Introduces the פסוק that proves the point

phrases.english: As it is taught:
From where for one who buys a field from his father
and consecrated it, and afterward his father died,
from where do we know that it is considered for him like an ancestral field?
The verse says:
"If a field that he bought
which is not of his ancestral field."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִן לְלוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the premise in Step 20 that רבי שמעון follows the time of פדיון.
steps.raayaObject: The premise that רבי שמעון judges a consecrated field by its status at the time of פדיון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא learning from ויקרא 27:22 about a son who bought his father's field.

steps.title: How the פסוק is read, and who holds this view
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks only of a field that could never become ancestral. That excludes this field, which was fit to become ancestral. This is the view of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse means a field that is not fit to become an ancestral field. That excludes this one, which is fit to become an ancestral field. These are the words of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the פסוק teaches its rule, and names the חכמים who hold it. One of them is רבי שמעון, which is why the גמרא quoted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'which is not of his ancestral field' are read narrowly: the purchased-field rules apply only to land that could never be inherited. A field bought from one's father was always going to come to him, so once the father dies it gets the שדה אחוזה rules. Because רבי שמעון holds this, the גמרא sees him as caring about the field's status when it is redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit / suitable. Here: able to eventually become an ancestral field
Is excluded (literally 'went out') from the rule

steps.whyThisMatters: The name רבי שמעון here is what makes this ברייתא useful. It is the source for the claim in Step 20 that he follows the time of פדיון.

phrases.english: A field that is not fit
to be an ancestral field;
this one, which is fit, is excluded,
phrases.notes: A field bought from his father would have come to him through inheritance anyway.

phrases.english: to be an ancestral field;
these are the words of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from Step 21: how the פסוק is read and who holds this view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון treats the field according to its later status when it is redeemed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי מאיר reads the פסוק as being about a different order of events
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees. He says the פסוק is needed for a case where the father died first and only afterward the son consecrated the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: From where do we know about someone who bought a field from his father, and his father died, and afterward he consecrated it, that it is treated for him like an ancestral field?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי מאיר's different view. He uses the same פסוק for an earlier case: the father died before the son consecrated the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the פסוק's ancestral-field rule covers a field that was already inherited when it was consecrated. That suggests he looks at the moment of consecration. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון extended the rule even to a field that only became ancestral after it was consecrated.

keyTerms.meaning: A buyer, one who purchases
And afterward. The order of events is the whole point here

steps.confusionAlert: Read the order of events carefully! In Step 21 he consecrated it first and then the father died. Here the father died first and then he consecrated it. The two cases look almost the same, but the order is exactly what is being argued about.

phrases.english: רבי מאיר says:
From where for one who buys a field from his father,
and his father died, and afterward he consecrated it,
from where do we know that it is considered for him like an ancestral field?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לַלּוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו, וּמֵת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same ברייתא. רבי מאיר uses the פסוק for a case where the father died before the field was consecrated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the פסוק teaches that a field bought from one's father is treated as ancestral when the father died before the son consecrated it.
